use_cases.title: Add a task
use_cases.description: A user adds a new task to the todo list by entering a task title and submitting it with Enter, with the source defining the title input and Enter key submission as the promised creation path.
use_cases.summary: Create a new task from a typed title.
use_cases.value: Lets users capture a new todo item in the list with minimal effort.

cite.quote: User can type a task title and press Enter to add it to the list.

criteria.text: A task is added from a typed task title when the user presses Enter.

use_cases.title: Complete a task
use_cases.description: A user marks an existing task complete by clicking its checkbox, with completion reflected as the completed task state and a strikethrough presentation called out by the source.
use_cases.value: Lets users track which tasks are finished without removing them from the list.

cite.quote: User can click a checkbox to mark a task complete

criteria.text: Clicking a checkbox marks a task complete.

cite.quote: User can click a checkbox to mark a task complete

criteria.text: Completed tasks use a strikethrough style.

use_cases.title: Delete a task
use_cases.description: A user removes an existing task from the todo list by clicking the task's "x" control, with the source defining deletion as a direct action on the task card.
use_cases.summary: Remove an existing task from the list.
use_cases.value: Lets users discard tasks that are no longer needed.

cite.quote: click an "x" to delete a task.

criteria.text: Deleting a task is triggered by clicking an "x" control on the task.

cite.quote: click an "x" to delete a task.

use_cases.title: Resume tasks after page reload
use_cases.description: A user returns to the application after a page reload and finds their tasks still present, with the source explicitly promising persistence across reloads via localStorage.
use_cases.summary: Keep tasks available after reloading the page.
use_cases.value: Prevents task loss and avoids re-entry after a refresh or reopen.

use_cases.title: See a task's priority
use_cases.description: A user sees each task card display a small priority badge while the existing card UI, controls, and layout otherwise remain unchanged, with the source specifying High, Medium, and Low values and a default of Medium but no priority-editing flow.
use_cases.summary: View the priority shown on each task card.
use_cases.value: Helps users distinguish task importance without changing the existing task card interaction model.
